A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching renamed attack variants and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original SDEdit and LoRA experiments on CelebA-HQ and WikiArt, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, offset analyses, and purification examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional target-selection, cross-model, defense, prediction-error, and unknown-prompt experiments.

M1.justification: V1's UNet-only and joint VAE/UNet attacks correspond to ITA and ITA+ in v2. The encoded target image, operational loss components, and alternating LoRA fitting and projected image updates remain (v1 Equations 15–16 and Algorithm 2; v2 Equations 9–10 and Algorithm 1). The rewritten derivation does not establish a different attack algorithm.

E1.justification: CelebA-HQ, WikiArt, SDEdit, and LoRA remain the core coverage. V2 substantially expands tested deployment conditions through unknown training prompts, a community-supplied black-box case, and Gaussian-noise, JPEG, and resizing defenses beyond v1's SR-only purification scenario.

E2.justification: The main effectiveness comparison retains AdvDM, Photoguard, and Anti-DB. V2 additionally evaluates Photoguard's diffusion attack, labeled Photoguard+, in the memory comparison and targeted Anti-DB, labeled Anti-DB-T, in target-selection and prediction-error comparisons.

E3.justification: The original benchmark metrics, sample counts, and attack schedule remain. New protocols include the SD1.4/1.5/2.1 transfer matrix, SDEdit strength 0.4 instead of the main experiment's 0.3, and explicit resolution handling. The defense experiment changes from a WikiArt SR case to 20 CelebA-HQ images with multiple defenses and an explicitly increased 8/255 budget.

E4.justification: V2 removes the offset studies, standalone VAE-only ablation result, and iteration-N sweep; the UNet-only versus joint comparison remains. It adds target-image and pattern-density/contrast studies, UNet prediction-error analysis, cross-model robustness, unknown-prompt tests, and broader purification analysis (Sections 5.3–5.4 and Appendix B).

E5.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 explicitly reports averaging 100 random timestep samples per image for prediction-error estimation. V1's offset plots, including their unexplained variability marks, disappear. Neither version provides independent-run counts or confidence intervals for the main benchmark scores; the new sampling count does not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 retain identical baseline scores but revise both proposed-method rows under the retained main settings. For example, UNet-only/ITA CelebA-HQ MS-SSIM changes from 0.38 to 0.73, while joint/ITA+ CLIP-SIM changes from 68.83 to 67.47. V2 also adds transfer, defense, and memory results and removes the old offset and iteration-sweep results.

T1.justification: V1's unified likelihood framework, three theorems, finetuning proposition, Gaussian lemma, and associated proofs and reductions in Appendices A–C are removed. V2 replaces this account with a general targeted KL objective and target-distribution derivation in Section 3. This substantially changes the mathematical argument despite retaining the operational attacks.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion drop the claimed comprehensive theoretical framework and resolution of the offset problem. V2 instead defines its contributions around effective targeted attacks and memory-efficient implementation below 6GB, making practical accessibility central.

C2.justification: The offset-alignment explanation is replaced by target-pattern effects and a proposed mismatch between generative-model objectives and human judgments (v2 Appendix C). New qualifications address overly dense targets, unknown keywords, SD2.1 resolution mismatch, and distortion introduced by defenses themselves.

D1.justification: V2 expands memory implementation documentation and specifies checkpointing UNet down/mid/up blocks, whereas v1 describes checkpointing the VAE. Resource measurements change to 5.77GB and 1739 seconds for 20 images. Most implementation details move intact from Appendix D to A, but v1's own-method code URL is omitted; this does not establish that the code became unavailable.

R1.justification: V1 positions earlier attacks as suboptimal instances of its unifying framework. V2 instead credits prior AdvDM theory, contrasts ITA with targeted Anti-DB, and argues that model-optimal attacks need not produce the worst human-perceived images. This substantially revises research positioning; accompanying citation changes include VQVAE and Gaussian/resizing defense references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Memory efficiency becomes a separate main section, transfer and defense sections replace the main ablation section, and the appendices are reorganized. The attack variants are consistently renamed ITA and ITA+.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the opening illustration with a broader baseline comparison, removes offset/geometry and iteration-ablation displays, and adds memory, transfer, defense, target-selection, and black-box displays. The document layout also changes substantially. The existing appendix image galleries are largely retained with revised labels and placement.

improvement.justification: V2 provides better evidence about practical applicability: target-selection tests, cross-model evaluation, and unknown-prompt and defense experiments address questions largely untested in v1 and expose useful limitations. These gains are tempered by removal of the theorem-based account, VAE-only and iteration ablations, and the own-code link. Main-table revisions remain unexplained, and defense results use a larger perturbation budget. Overall, the practical evidence improves, but the net quality gain is limited.
